newsitem.title: UK: Framlington launches $25 mln West Africa fund.
newsitem.headline: Framlington launches $25 mln West Africa fund.

text.p: Investment management group Framlington said on Thursday it had launched a new specialist equity investment fund investing in West Africa.
London-based Framlington said the $25 million West Africa Growth Fund was supported by the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and Caisse Francaise de Developpement (CFD).
The IFC had subscribed for more than $6 million of the fund and had been an active adviser on the fund's structure and identification of investment opportunities.
The CFD group invested more than $5 million.
It said other institutional and private investors had subscribed, some of them from West Africa.
The fund aims to invest in quality growth companies operating predominantly in West Africa with an emphasis on six core economies of Ivory Coast, Cameroon, Senegal, Congo, Gabon and Mali.
Investments will be in listed, unlisted and recently privatised companies.
"Opportunities in neighbouring countries such as Ghana may also be assessed for potential investment if they fall within the scope of the investment policy," Framlington said.
The fund is listed in Luxembourg as a SICAV, and plans a second listing in Abidjan, Ivory Coast.

Framlington Institutional managing director Jean-Luc Schilling said the fund would allow investors to benefit from the growth, cheap asset prices and opportunities created by ongoing privatisation programmes.
He said the region offered attractive potential returns with the evolving free trade zone having a common currency in the CFA franc.
